text: Does bespoke metabolic investigation reduce urinary stone recurrence? A narrative review. To examine whether individualised ('bespoke') metabolic investigation and targeted dietary and medical therapy reduces urinary stone recurrence, and whether the approach also improves health-related quality of life (HRQOL) and lowers financial and environmental cost.

An artificial intelligence model combining MRI and ultrasound images (MRUSuNet) for prostate cancer detection outperforms radiologist MRI interpretation. To develop the magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-UltraSound UNet (MRUSuNet), a model that uses both MRI and transrectal ultrasonography (TRUS) as input to detect and localise the three-dimensional spatial volume of clinically significant prostate cancer on TRUS images to allow better visualisation of cancer in the TRUS space.

Clinical Outcomes of Bladder-sparing Management Versus Early Radical Cystectomy in cT1 Micropapillary Bladder Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Clinical T1 micropapillary urothelial carcinoma of the bladder is an aggressive variant histology for which early radical cystectomy (RC) is commonly recommended. However, there remain conflicting data on whether conditions in carefully selected patients may be managed with initial bladder-sparing approaches without compromising oncologic outcomes.

Radiolabelled cyclodextrins to detect cervical cancer: a preclinical feasibility study. Radiolabelled cyclodextrins targeting prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) seem promising candidates for positron emission tomography (PET)-based molecular imaging of cervical cancer. Here, we evaluated the performance of gallium-68-labelled 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HPβCD) and randomly methylated β-cyclodextrin (RAMEB) for the in vivo PET detection of cervical cancer. P-glycoprotein positive (Pgp+) KB-V-1 and P-glycoprotein negative (Pgp-) KB-3-1 cervical carcinoma xenografts of varying sizes (small-, medium-, large-sized) were established and subjected to [68Ga]Ga-NODAGA-HPβCD and [68Ga]Ga-DOTAGA-RAMEB PET imaging followed by ex vivo biodistribution and immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis of PGE2 and Pgp expression. In line with the IHC results, PET data revealed the capability of both radiotracers to reliably detect each tumor types independent of tumor size. Nevertheless, the modest increase in uptake observed with increasing size may indicate enhanced tumor aggressiveness and angiogenic activity. Comparable radiotracer accumulation in MDR-positive and MDR-negative tumors suggests that HPβCD and RAMEB derivatives are unlikely to serve as substrates of Pgp enabling tumor detection across different tumor types. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that radiolabelled cyclodextrins are promising PET tracers for the in vivo detection of cervical cancer, irrespective of tumor size and Pgp expression.
